Remove one (1) Araucaria heterophylla (Norfolk Island Pine), one (1) unknown species and one (1) Radermachera sinica (China Doll) from the front yard and replace with three (3) small-sized local native trees from Council’s Development Control Plan 2022, Annexure B3-2 Tree Canopy Replacement Planting List, of minimum 45L pot size, anywhere on the property, within one (1) month of removal. Norfolk Island Pine: This tree is growing out of a raised soil mound and is in an inappropriate and unsustainable location. It is only a small specimen however it has the potential to reach massive proportions. The limited soil volume will be unable to sustain the tree's mature proportions, it is highly probable that the tree will impact the front boundary fence and/or fail entirely due to limited space for it to develop anchoring roots. It is recommended that it be removed and replaced as soon as possible. Unknown species: This tree is impacting the corner of the front boundary fences which it is growing out from underneath. The wall is in a state of disrepair, conduct the works the tree will need to be removed. China Doll: This tree has the potential to reach massive proportions, it is only small however it has poor structure, it has co-dominant stems and is growing within proximity to the front boundary fence which it will inevitably damage as its trunks expand. - Waverley Council TPO-40/2026

Remove three (3) Cupressus sempervirens (Mediterranean Cypress) T1, T2, T3 from the front of the property, remove one (1) Ulmus sp (Elm tree) T4 from the southside of the property and remove two (2) Ulmus sp (Elm tree) T5, T6 from the south rear of the property. T1 - Conifer: This tree is adjacent to a water pipe, a cracked footpath, and a small front boundary wall which is collapsing toward the public footpath, repairs to the wall can only be carried out with this tree's removal. Remove and replace. T2 - Conifer: This tree is in fair health, only the upper portion of its canopy has leaves, the lower half is mostly deadwood and bare, woody branches. This tree has low retention value, remove and replace. T3 - Conifer: The applicant's reason for this tree's removal is regarding damage to structures. The tree is situated almost a metre away from the building line and was in good health at the time of inspection. While the building and driveway slabs had cracks, the structures are old - their disrepair cannot be solely attributed to damage from tree roots, rather the primary cause of their failure appears to be their age. The repair works should be conducted with the tree's retainment. Should the repairs require the tree's removal, additional information is required in the form of a structural engineer's report. Please refer to Council’s website for details on what to include in the report: https://www.waverley.nsw.gov.au/residents/your_trees,_plants_and_garden/tree_pruning_and_removal T4 - Elm (not Camphor): This tree is deciduous - at the time of inspection it had no leaves. It is situated in the centre of the garden bed, its trunk and canopy are a sufficient distance away from surrounding structures, there was no structural damage observed, no works are required at this time. Removal refused. T5 & T6: - Elm: These two trees are deciduous - at the time of inspection they had no leaves. Their trunks are up against the boundary fence and are growing around a small brick retaining wall which has compromised their trunks' natural structure, impacting their stability and structural integrity as they mature and creating a potential hazard. Remove and replace. Replacement Tree requirements: four (4) local native trees from Council’s Preferred Tree list, of minimum 45L pot size, growing to similar dimensions at maturity, anywhere on the property, within one (1) month of removal. - Waverley Council TPO-207/2025

Remove one (1) Frangipani in the front yard and replace with one small/medium-sized (1) local native tree from Council’s Development Control Plan 2022, Annexure B3-2 Tree Canopy Replacement Planting List, of minimum 45L pot size, anywhere on the property, within one (1) month of removal. At the time of inspection this mature tree was deciduous and had good form and structure, there were new season buds present. The issue however is with the tree's roots and the damage to the plumbing - the plumber's investigation revealed "After digging down in the soil, we found the 20mm copper cold water service had cracked and the unions on the water meter were leaking as the meter has raised. This has been caused by the tree root within the garden bed, putting stress on the pipe work". - Waverley Council TPO-206/2025
